paragraphs: Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosi ben Lakunya.

[Shevuot 18b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.18b.4) (18a in Hyman’s citation) relates that he asked Rabbi Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya a question, and Rabbi Shimon picked up a stone and threw it at him. Hyman says the Gemara contains a textual error and should read as in [Jerusalem Talmud Horayot 2:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Horayot.2.5.4): R' Yonatan asked R' Shimon, son of R' Yose ben Lakunya, and R' Shimon wanted to throw a stone after him.

notes.text: The notice’s heading attaches Yose and Lakunya to Yonatan. Its proposed Jerusalem Talmud reading instead has Yonatan asking Shimon, whose father is Yose and ancestor Lakunya. Horayot2:5 says Shimon wanted to throw a stone, contrasting with the notice’s account of the Bavli as an actual throw. No family reconstruction is adopted.

[Heilprin’s related entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1929&lang=en) also flags variant names and directs readers to Yonatan’s and Shimon’s notices. The attribution and the act of throwing differ between the two linked passages.

Hyman’s print cites Shevuot 18a. The consulted passage at 18b calls both Yonatan and Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya, and Shimon throws a clod at Yonatan. Jerusalem Talmud Horayot 2:5 has Yonatan send the question to Shimon, son of Rabbi Yose bar Lakunya. It gives Yonatan no patronymic in this exchange, and Shimon wants to throw a stone. Hyman’s proposed correction is preserved alongside both accounts.
